data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim that the bounded harness outperforms single calls 'only when the temperature is high' is contradicted by its own mechanism description. The mechanism states the harness prevents 'drift from accumulating into total nonsense.' In low-temperature settings, while individual steps are more coherent, multi-step reasoning without structural anchoring still suffers from compounding minor errors or logical gaps (a form of drift) that a single continuous generation might gloss over. By restricting the benefit strictly to high temperatures, the target ignores the harness's value in enforcing rigorous step-wise validity even when the model is confident, thus failing to accurately characterize the conditions under which the harness produces better surviving conjectures.
